scope: Phase B engineering implementation for development-quality feedback, explicit quality-limit status, and valid-ready RTL verification; no formal research experiment and no evaluator-formula correction

changes.result: Rule-based and LLM proposers share an accepted/rejected/inconclusive evaluator protocol. Measured rejection feedback is retained and supplied to the next attempt; evaluator exceptions stop as inconclusive.
Measurement success is separated from satisfaction of the explicit numerical limit. The public synthetic-tone decision is labeled development_only with deployment_acceptance=false.
RTL outputs are checked in accepted-transaction order without a fixed latency assumption. Input gaps, output backpressure, stalled-output stability, and a maximum-cycle progress bound are exercised.

verification.interpretation: All search_ir tests present in the working tree passed.

verification.observed_summary: 1382 passed, 5 failed, 17 errors, 43 subtests passed in 138.49s
verification.limitations: The remaining failures/errors were outside the changed search_ir path and included inability to bind the optillm integration-test ports in the sandbox, missing socksio for SOCKS-proxy provider tests, and a missing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY required by configuration-validation tests. This run is not reported as a full-suite pass.

verification.observed_summary: collection stopped because an unrelated example imports unavailable mlx
verification.interpretation: No full-repository pass claim is made.

limitations: The feedback loop currently uses one public development fixture and quality only; it does not consume synthesis area, static timing, Q_main, or held-out results.
The transaction checker is latency-independent by construction, but no alternative-latency generated implementation exists yet, so cross-microarchitecture compatibility is not yet demonstrated.
This implementation changes orchestration and verification status, not the numerical evaluator formula; AUDIT.md was therefore not changed.
No result in this record establishes that an LLM proposer outperforms a traditional search method.
